artworks.title: Poseidon Fighting Polybotes
artworks.description: Tondo of an Attic red-figure kylix (Cabinet des Médailles, Paris): Poseidon spears the Giant Polybotes while carrying the island of Nisyros on his shoulder — the myth that explains the volcanic islet off Cos. The Painter of the Paris Gigantomachy makes Polybotes the sea-god's named antagonist.

artworks.title: Mosaic of Poseidon and the Giant Polybotes
artworks.description: A mosaic in the Palace of the Grand Master, Rhodes, restages Poseidon against Polybotes — the Giant chased through the sea and buried under the broken island. Floor art keeps the Cos–Nisyros etiology vivid in the Dodecanese.

popCulture.title: Nisyros
popCulture.description: The volcanic island Poseidon tore from Cos to crush Polybotes — the Giant's prison still steaming in the Aegean.

popCulture.title: Polybotes
popCulture.description: Earthborn Giant whom Poseidon pursued and buried under Nisyros — one of the named antagonists of the Gigantomachy.

popCulture.title: Gigantomachy
popCulture.description: The battle of gods and Giants in which Polybotes falls to Poseidon — the cosmic war carved on temples and painted on cups.
